questions.question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

If you had spoken to my mother, she would tell you where I was.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a **third conditional sentence**, which is used to describe hypothetical situations in the past.
 
• The structure of the third conditional is **"If + past perfect, would have + past participle"**.
 
• In the result clause of the conditional sentence, the verb should be in the form **"would have + past participle"**.
 
• However, the verb **"tell"** in the result clause is incorrect and should be replaced with **"would have told"**.

Correct sentence: *If you had spoken to my mother, she **would have told** you where I was*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage: **Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were rich, I would travel the world.
 
• **Usage: **Describes hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present or future.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure: **If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example: **If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage: **Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.

• **Option 1:** "on that tree" suggests the puppy is physically on top of the tree, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 2:** "across that tree" implies moving from one side of the tree to another, which is incorrect here.
 
• **Option 3:** "around that tree" is the most appropriate as it matches the intended meaning of movement near or encircling the tree.
 
• **Option 4:** "No substitution" is incorrect as the original phrase needs correction.
 
 

Correct sentence: *I don't understand why the puppy keeps running around that tree*.

• **"On":** Indicates physical contact with a surface. Example: The book is on the table.
 
• **"Across":** Refers to movement from one side to the other. Example: He swam across the river.
 
• **"Around":** Suggests movement in a circular or surrounding manner. Example: They walked around the park.
 
 
 
• Choosing the correct preposition depends on the context and the action being described.

options.text: Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to throw out of the house with your maximum strength.

• The sentence is in the imperative form, and the passive voice of an imperative sentence typically begins with "Let."
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject.
 
• The correct structure for the passive voice in this sentence is: **Let + object + be + past participle**.
 
• The second part of the sentence, "you have to throw the entire thing out of the house with your maximum strength," is converted to passive voice as "the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength."

• **Imperative Active Voice:** Cut the wire. → **Passive Voice:** Let the wire be cut.
 
• **Present Simple Active Voice:** She throws the ball. → **Passive Voice:** The ball is thrown by her.
 
• **Future Simple Active Voice:** He will complete the project. → **Passive Voice:** The project will be completed by him.
 
 
 
• **Note:** Always ensure the correct placement of "by" and the subject when converting sentences to passive voice.

Rajan said to Rini, "I have very often informed you that we have to attend the meeting every Saturday."

__
 
• The sentence is in direct speech and needs to be converted to indirect speech.
 
• When converting direct speech into indirect speech:
 
 
• The verb tense changes based on the reporting verb (past tense here).
 
• Pronouns are adjusted according to the context of the sentence.
 
• Words indicating time or frequency, such as "very often" and "every Saturday," remain unchanged as they do not affect the tense.
 
 
 
• The direct speech, "I have very often informed you that we have to attend the meeting every Saturday," becomes "Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday." This is because:
 
 
• "Have informed" changes to "had informed" (past perfect tense).
 
• "You" changes to "her" (adjusted for the listener).
 
• "We" changes to "they" (adjusted for the speaker and listener).
 
 

Correct sentence: *Rajan told Rini that he had very often informed her that they had to attend the meeting every Saturday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for changing direct to indirect speech:**
 
 
• If the reporting verb is in the past tense, the verb in the reported clause must be changed to a corresponding past form.
 
• Personal pronouns must be adjusted to reflect the speaker and listener.
 
• Time expressions such as "today," "tomorrow," "yesterday" may need to be changed based on the context.
 
 
 
• **Examples of tense changes in indirect speech:**
 
 
• Simple Present → Simple Past
 
• Present Perfect → Past Perfect
 
• Simple Past → Past Perfect

Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Dinner is being prepared by my sister.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**, as indicated by the use of "is being prepared."
 
• To change a sentence from passive to active voice, the subject performing the action must be placed at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The subject in this case is "my sister," and the action being performed is "preparing dinner."
 
• The correct active voice structure is: **Subject + is/am/are + verb + object**.

Correct sentence: *My sister is preparing dinner*.

• **Passive Voice Structure:** Object + is/am/are + being + past participle + by + subject.

 
 
• Example: The book is being read by John.
 
 
 
• **Active Voice Structure:** Subject + is/am/are + verb + object.
 
 
• Example: John is reading the book.
 
 
 
• Option 1: "Dinner prepared my sister" is grammatically incorrect because "prepared" is in the past tense and the structure does not properly indicate the action.
 
• Option 3: "My sister prepares dinner" is in the present simple tense, which does not correspond to the continuous action implied by "is being prepared."

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **indirect speech**, where a question is being reported.
 
• To convert indirect speech into direct speech for a question, the sentence must:
 
 
• Include quotation marks.
 
• Use the exact question format and wording.
 
• Retain the original tense of the question.
 
 
 
• In direct speech, the question is typically introduced with a reporting verb like "said to" or "asked."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for converting indirect speech to direct speech:**

 
 
• Remove introductory words like "He asked me" or "He said."
 
• Use quotation marks to enclose the exact words spoken.
 
• Ensure proper punctuation, such as a question mark for questions.
 
• Preserve the tense from the original direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Indirect: She asked if I was coming tomorrow. → Direct: She asked, "Are you coming tomorrow?"
 
• Indirect: He wondered whether it was raining. → Direct: He said, "Is it raining?"

questions.question: Which sentence from the passage is written in the present perfect tense?

options.text: Every hospital employee plays a critical role.
Many remain committed to their work.
Awareness about the importance of every hospital worker has grown.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **Present Perfect Tense**, we look for the specific verb structure: **Has/Have + Past Participle (V3)**.
 
• In **Option 4**, the sentence "Awareness... **has grown**" follows this exact formula (*has* + the third form of the verb *grow*). This tense is used to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or began in the past and continues to the present.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Hospitals **operate**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1).
 
• **Option 2:** "...employee **plays**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1 + s).
 
• **Option 3:** "Many **remain**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, identifying tenses is a foundational skill. Always remember that the Present Perfect ("has grown") links the past to the present, whereas the Simple Past ("grew") would imply the action is finished and disconnected from now.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Three vessels X, Y, and Z hold liquid in the capacity ratio of 3:4:5. Each vessel contains a mixture of juice and water, where the proportions are 1:2 in X, 3:1 in Y, and 2:3 in Z. Vessel capacities: X = 3 units, Y = 4 units, Z = 5 units.

Total ratio parts: X (1+2=3), Y (3+1=4), Z (2+3=5).

Since capacity matches the total parts, add components directly.

Total Juice = 1 (from X) + 3 (from Y) + 2 (from Z) = 6 units.

Total Water = 2 (from X) + 1 (from Y) + 3 (from Z) = 6 units.

**∴ Answer = 1 : 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Capacity ratio X : Y : Z = 3 : 4 : 5

Ratio of Juice : Water in X = 1 : 2 (Total parts = 3)

Ratio of Juice : Water in Y = 3 : 1 (Total parts = 4)

Ratio of Juice : Water in Z = 2 : 3 (Total parts = 5)

**Formula used:**

Total Juice = sum of juice in all vessels; Total Water = sum of water in all vessels.

 X(3L) 1:2 Y(4L) 3:1 Z(5L) 2:3 
• 
 Mix(12L) 6 : 6 Ratio = 1 : 1 Juice Water 

**Calculations:**

Let the volumes of vessels X, Y, and Z be 3L, 4L, and 5L respectively.

⇒ Juice in X = 3 × (1/3) = 1L; Water in X = 3 − 1 = 2L

⇒ Juice in Y = 4 × (3/4) = 3L; Water in Y = 4 − 3 = 1L

⇒ Juice in Z = 5 × (2/5) = 2L; Water in Z = 5 − 2 = 3L

⇒ Total Juice = 1 + 3 + 2 = 6L

⇒ Total Water = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6L

⇒ Final Ratio = Total Juice : Total Water = 6 : 6 = 1 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 1 (Option 3).**

__

• The **Malhotra Committee** was formed in **1993** by the Government of India to suggest reforms in the **insurance sector**.

• The committee was chaired by **R.N. Malhotra**, the former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

• It submitted its report in the year **1994**, recommending several pivotal changes to liberalize and modernize the Indian insurance sector.

• The report emphasized the need for opening up the insurance sector to **private players** and the establishment of an independent **regulatory authority** to oversee insurance activities.

• The recommendations of the Malhotra Committee laid the groundwork for the formation of the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in 1999.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Key Recommendations of the Malhotra Committee:**

• Opening up the Indian insurance market to **private sector** participation to foster competition and efficiency.

• Introducing **foreign direct investment (FDI)** in the insurance sector, with a cap of 26% initially, which was later increased to 49% and subsequently to 74% in 2021.

• Establishing an independent regulatory body, which resulted in the creation of the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in 1999.

• Allowing private companies to enter both **life insurance** and **non-life insurance** sectors.

• Restructuring the public sector insurance companies to operate on a more competitive basis.

• **Impact of the Malhotra Committee Report:**

• The recommendations led to the liberalization of the Indian insurance market in the **early 2000s**.

• Private sector players like **HDFC Life, ICICI Lombard, Max Life**, and others entered the market, increasing competition and improving service quality.

• The establishment of IRDAI brought about **transparency** and **uniform regulations** for the insurance sector.

• Insurance penetration in India improved significantly, with more people opting for life and non-life insurance policies.

• **About R.N. Malhotra:**

• **R.N. Malhotra** served as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from **1985 to 1990**.

• He was instrumental in shaping financial reforms in India and played a key role in the liberalization process of the insurance sector.

• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**

• Established in **1999** as an independent regulatory body to oversee insurance activities in India.

• Its objectives include protecting the interests of policyholders, promoting healthy competition, and ensuring the financial stability of the insurance market.

• **Liberalization of the Insurance Sector:**

• The entry of private players and FDI brought technological advancements and customer-centric services to the industry.

• Insurance penetration increased from **2.15% (2001)** to **4.2% (2021)**, as per IRDAI reports.

questions.question: What subject does Article 77 of the Indian Constitution pertain to?

options.text: Conduct of business of the Government of India
Council of Ministers to aid and advise President

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conduct of business of the Government of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 77 of the Indian Constitution** pertains to the **conduct of business of the Government of India**. It outlines how the executive actions and decisions of the Government are to be carried out.
 
• It states that all executive actions of the Government of India should be expressed in the name of the **President of India**.
 
• It also specifies the rules for the allocation of business among the different **Ministries and Departments** of the Government.
 
• The President is empowered to make rules for the more convenient transaction of business and for its distribution among the Ministers.
 
• This Article ensures that the functioning of the Government is streamlined, organized, and accountable under the framework of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **President's Role in Executive Actions:**

 
 
• All executive actions of the Government of India are performed in the name of the **President**, as per Article 77.
 
• The **President** acts on the advice of the **Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This ensures that the executive authority is exercised within the framework of parliamentary democracy.
 
 
 
• **Rules for Allocation of Business:**
 
 
• The President has the authority to frame rules for the allocation of business among the **Ministers**.
 
• These rules are crucial for ensuring the **smooth functioning** of the Government and avoiding overlapping responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Accountability in Governance:**
 
 
• Article 77 mandates that all executive actions be conducted transparently, ensuring **accountability** to the Parliament and the citizens.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a clear and organized system for executing the policies and decisions of the Government.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Article 74:**
 
 
• While Article 77 deals with the conduct of business, **Article 74** deals with the Council of Ministers aiding and advising the President.
 
• Both Articles collectively ensure the smooth operation of the **executive branch** of the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• All official communications, like **notifications and orders**, are issued in the name of the President.
 
• For instance, appointment letters for high-ranking officials like Governors and Supreme Court judges bear the President’s name.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 77 and Parliamentary Democracy:**

 
 
• Article 77 is integral to India's system of **parliamentary democracy**, where the executive is accountable to the legislature.
 
• It ensures a uniform system for the **execution of policies and legal frameworks** as determined by the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework for Ministries:**
 
 
• This Article provides a legal basis for the formation and functioning of various **Ministries** and **Departments** within the Government.
 
• It enables Ministers to act within their allocated portfolios and ensures **clarity in decision-making**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Article 77 was drafted as part of the Constitution of India, which came into effect on **26 January 1950**.
 
• The Article was inspired by the British system of governance and adapted to fit India’s parliamentary model.

questions.question: Members of the Legislative Council of an Indian state as nearly as may be, ____ shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1/3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 171** of the Constitution of India specifies the composition of the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) for states that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• As per **Article 171(3)(a)**, **1/3 of the members** of the Legislative Council are elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities in the state.
 
• The provision ensures representation from local self-governing bodies, which play a vital role in state governance.
 
• These members are chosen through an electoral process where representatives from various local bodies vote to elect Legislative Council members.
 
• This mechanism provides a democratic way to include local governance in the legislative process, fostering decentralized decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Legislative Council:**

 
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house of the state legislature in states with bicameral legislatures (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka).
 
• Its members are elected, nominated, or indirectly appointed through various processes outlined in Article 171.
 
• The Council must not exceed **one-third** of the total membership of the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
 
 
• **Election Process:**
 
 
• Members elected by local authorities constitute **1/3** of the total members of the Legislative Council.
 
• Other members are elected by graduates, teachers, members of the Legislative Assembly, or nominated by the Governor.
 
• The election process is conducted by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Role of Local Authorities:**
 
 
• Local authorities such as municipalities and district boards play a significant role in state governance.
 
• Representation from local bodies ensures that issues relevant to local administration are addressed in the state legislature.
 
• This system strengthens participatory democracy by incorporating grassroots-level governance into the legislative framework.
 
 
 
• **States with Legislative Councils:**
 
 
• Currently, only **6 states** in India have Legislative Councils: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
 
• States can propose the creation or abolition of Legislative Councils, but the final decision rests with Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The bicameral system in state legislatures was established to include diverse perspectives in law-making.
 
• The inclusion of local authorities in the election process reflects the significance of grassroots governance in India.
 
• It was introduced to balance representation from different sections of society and administrative units.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 171:** Defines the composition and electoral process for Legislative Councils in states with bicameral legislatures.
 
• **Representation:** Ensures inclusion of local self-governance bodies in the legislative process through elections.
 
• **Governor’s Role:** The Governor nominates 1/6th of the members of the Legislative Council, typically experts in various fields like literature, science, or social service.
 
• **Election Eligibility:** Members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities are eligible to vote in the elections for Legislative Council members.
 
• **Relevance:** Legislative Councils provide an additional layer of checks and balances in state governance, complementing the Legislative Assembly.
